title: Teaching Models to Express Their Uncertainty in Words
contribution: Fine-tunes GPT-3 to state calibrated numeric or word-level confidence without logits and introduces the CalibratedMath suite

title: Reducing conversational agents' overconfidence through linguistic calibration
contribution: Pairs a correctness calibrator with controllable generation so a chat agent's hedging level matches its chance of being right

title: Just Ask for Calibration: Strategies for Eliciting Calibrated Confidence Scores from Language Models Fine-Tuned with Human Feedback
family: verbalised numeric, linguistic and top-k prompting
contribution: Shows prompted verbalised confidences, including top-k and linguistic variants, are better calibrated than token probabilities for RLHF chat models

title: Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation in LLMs
contribution: Benchmarks black-box elicitation strategies built from prompting, sampling and aggregation and finds verbalised confidence overconfident but improvable

title: Navigating the Grey Area: How Expressions of Uncertainty and Overconfidence Affect Language Models
contribution: Shows that expressions of certainty and uncertainty in prompts shift LM accuracy, with high-certainty markers hurting performance

title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
contribution: Shows large LMs are calibrated on multiple-choice and can self-evaluate sampled answers via a P(True) prompt, plus a trained P(IK) head

title: Relying on the Unreliable: The Impact of Language Models' Reluctance to Express Uncertainty
contribution: Finds LMs rarely hedge, are overconfident when they do, and that users over-rely on confident phrasing, linking the bias to preference data

title: I'm Not Sure, But...: Examining the Impact of Large Language Models' Uncertainty Expression on User Reliance and Trust
contribution: Large user study showing first-person uncertainty phrases lower over-reliance and raise task accuracy in information seeking

title: What Large Language Models Know and What People Think They Know
family: calibration gap between model and human confidence
contribution: Shows users overestimate LLM accuracy from default explanations and that wording matched to model confidence narrows the calibration and discrimination gaps

title: Can Large Language Models Faithfully Express Their Intrinsic Uncertainty in Words?
contribution: Defines faithfulness of verbal hedging as the gap between assertion decisiveness and intrinsic confidence and finds LLMs unfaithful even when prompted

title: Quantifying Uncertainty in Natural Language Explanations of Large Language Models
family: verbalised and probing uncertainty of explanations
contribution: Proposes verbalised and perturbation-based probing uncertainty for LLM explanations and finds verbalised confidence unreliable

title: Overconfidence is Key: Verbalized Uncertainty Evaluation in Large Language and Vision-Language Models
family: verbalised uncertainty evaluation in LLMs and VLMs
contribution: Evaluates verbalised confidence of LLMs and VLMs across tasks with a signed net calibration error and finds pervasive overconfidence

title: When Do LLMs Need Retrieval Augmentation? Mitigating LLMs' Overconfidence Helps Retrieval Augmentation
contribution: Quantifies overconfidence of prompted certainty and uses it to trigger retrieval augmentation only when the model is unsure

title: On Verbalized Confidence Scores for LLMs
family: prompt design for verbalised confidence scores
contribution: Large study of prompt variants for verbalised confidence scores, identifying designs that improve calibration at low cost

title: Fact-and-Reflection (FaR) Improves Confidence Calibration of Large Language Models
contribution: Proposes Fact-and-Reflection prompting that elicits facts and reflects before answering, lowering verbalised-confidence ECE

title: Calibrating Verbalized Probabilities for Large Language Models
family: verbalised class distributions with invert-softmax scaling
contribution: Elicits verbalised label distributions and fixes re-softmax distortion with an invert-softmax trick before temperature scaling

title: Factual Confidence of LLMs: on Reliability and Robustness of Current Estimators
contribution: Compares verbalised, consistency, logit and trained-probe estimators of factual confidence and tests robustness to paraphrase

title: Confidence in the Reasoning of Large Language Models
contribution: Measures LLM confidence as persistence under a reconsider prompt and as a self-reported score, finding both poorly tied to accuracy

title: Large Language Models are overconfident and amplify human bias
contribution: Applies human overconfidence protocols to LLMs and finds they overestimate their correctness by 20 to 60 percent, more than humans

title: Mind the Confidence Gap: Overconfidence, Calibration, and Distractor Effects in Large Language Models
contribution: Studies verbalised overconfidence across model sizes and shows that adding distractor options changes calibration

title: Revisiting Epistemic Markers in Confidence Estimation: Can Markers Accurately Reflect Large Language Models' Uncertainty?
contribution: Defines marker confidence as observed accuracy per epistemic marker and finds markers stable in-domain but inconsistent out of distribution

title: Are LLM-Judges Robust to Expressions of Uncertainty? Investigating the effect of Epistemic Markers on LLM-based Evaluation
contribution: Shows LLM judges are biased against responses carrying uncertainty markers regardless of correctness

title: Rel-A.I.: An Interaction-Centered Approach To Measuring Human-LM Reliance
contribution: Introduces Rel-A.I. to measure human reliance on LM statements and shows context and warm or hedged phrasing strongly shape reliance

title: Perceptions of Linguistic Uncertainty by Language Models and Humans
contribution: Compares how LLMs and humans map uncertainty expressions to probabilities and finds LLM interpretations biased by their own beliefs

title: An Evaluation of Estimative Uncertainty in Large Language Models
contribution: Compares LLM and human numeric readings of words of estimative probability and tests LLM use of them for uncertain events

title: Combining Confidence Elicitation and Sample-based Methods for Uncertainty Quantification in Misinformation Mitigation
contribution: Combines direct confidence elicitation with sample-based consistency for misinformation classification and studies their calibration

title: Measuring short-form factuality in large language models
contribution: Introduces SimpleQA and measures calibration by comparing stated confidence and answer frequency with accuracy

title: Self-Evaluation Improves Selective Generation in Large Language Models
contribution: Reformulates open generation as multi-way or point-wise self-evaluation so token-level scores drive selective generation

title: Calibrating the Confidence of Large Language Models by Eliciting Fidelity
contribution: Decomposes confidence into uncertainty about the question and fidelity to the answer, giving a plug-and-play calibration method

title: Do Large Language Models Know What They Don't Know?
contribution: Introduces SelfAware and detects uncertainty phrasing in responses to measure whether LLMs recognise unanswerable questions

title: Confidence Under the Hood: An Investigation into the Confidence-Probability Alignment in Large Language Models
contribution: Measures alignment between token-probability confidence and verbally stated certainty across prompting techniques

title: Calibration and Correctness of Language Models for Code
family: calibration of code models incl. reflective prompts
contribution: Studies intrinsic and reflective confidence for code generation and shows Platt scaling is needed for usable calibration

title: Confidence Estimation for LLM-Based Dialogue State Tracking
contribution: Compares softmax, raw token, verbalised and combined confidence for LLM dialogue state tracking

title: Confidence Matters: Revisiting Intrinsic Self-Correction Capabilities of Large Language Models
contribution: Shows LLMs can gauge confidence in their answers and proposes an If-or-Else prompt that revises only low-confidence answers

title: MetaFaith: Faithful Natural Language Uncertainty Expression in LLMs
contribution: Large study showing LLM hedges are unfaithful to intrinsic uncertainty and proposes metacognitive prompts that improve faithfulness

title: Epistemic Integrity in Large Language Models
contribution: Builds a human-labelled assertiveness dataset and scorer and shows LLM assertiveness is misaligned with internal certainty

title: Accounting for Sycophancy in Language Model Uncertainty Estimation
contribution: Studies how user suggestions bias model confidence and proposes SyRoUP to account for sycophancy in uncertainty estimates

title: Probing neural language models for understanding of words of estimative probability
contribution: Probes whether LMs understand words of estimative probability via consensus and reasoning tasks

title: Humans overrely on overconfident language models, across languages
contribution: Shows LLMs are overconfident across five languages and that human reliance on hedges and boosters differs by language

title: Reasoning Models Better Express Their Confidence
contribution: Finds long chain-of-thought reasoning models express better calibrated confidence, traced to slow-thinking behaviours

title: Reasoning about Uncertainty: Do Reasoning Models Know When They Don't Know?
contribution: Evaluates whether reasoning models are calibrated in verbalised confidence and whether introspection or deeper reasoning helps

title: Are Large Language Models More Honest in Their Probabilistic or Verbalized Confidence?
contribution: Compares token-probability and verbalised perception of factual knowledge boundaries and how each varies with question frequency

title: The Confidence-Competence Gap in Large Language Models: A Cognitive Study
contribution: Compares LLM self-assessed confidence with actual performance and reports Dunning-Kruger-like patterns

title: Think Twice Before Trusting: Self-Detection for Large Language Models through Comprehensive Answer Reflection
contribution: Proposes Think Twice before Trusting, which reflects on multiple candidate answers to curb over-trust in self-detection

title: Calibrating Long-form Generations from Large Language Models
contribution: Treats correctness and confidence as distributions for long-form outputs, adds self-evaluation and consistency elicitation and a cascade use case

title: MlingConf: A Comprehensive Study of Multilingual Confidence Estimation on Large Language Models
contribution: Benchmarks LLM confidence estimation across languages and finds language dominance effects in calibration

title: Calibrating Verbalized Confidence with Self-Generated Distractors
contribution: Normalises verbalised confidence by confidence on self-generated distractor claims to correct suggestibility-driven overconfidence

title: Can Large Language Models Express Uncertainty Like Human?
family: linguistic confidence via hedges and a mapper
contribution: Releases a human-annotated hedge-confidence dataset and mapper and studies prompted linguistic confidence across LLMs

title: Not All Uncertainty Is Equal: How Uncertainty Granularity Shapes Human Verification in LLM-Assisted Decision Making
contribution: User study comparing output-level, claim-level and token-level uncertainty displays for verification in LLM-assisted decisions

title: Can LLMs Use Linguistic Uncertainty Markers to Reliably Reflect Intrinsic Confidence?
contribution: Formalises marker internal confidence and tests whether LLMs map their own epistemic markers to stable confidence levels

title: ConfidenceBench: Evaluating Confidence Calibration in Large Language Models
contribution: Private multiple-choice benchmark scoring prompted verbalised confidence of frontier LLMs with the Brier score

title: Overconfidence in LLM-as-a-Judge: Diagnosis and Confidence-Driven Solution
contribution: Diagnoses overconfidence in LLM judges, proposes the TH-Score metric and an LLM-as-a-Fuser ensemble

title: Rethinking Verbalized Confidence for LLM-as-a-Judge: A Compatibility Shift on Post-2025 Proprietary Models
contribution: Shows verbalised confidence beats log-probabilities as a judge score on post-2025 proprietary models and adds overconfidence advisory and self-debate

title: Are LLM Decisions Faithful to Verbal Confidence?
contribution: Introduces RiskEval and finds models neither adjust verbal confidence nor abstention to error penalties

title: Let the Model Distribute Its Doubt: Confidence Estimation through Verbalized Probability Distribution
contribution: Prompts for a probability distribution over all candidate answers, which improves reasoning for confidence estimation

title: On the Robustness of Verbal Confidence of LLMs in Adversarial Attacks
contribution: Designs perturbation and jailbreak attacks that degrade verbal confidence and shows current defences are weak

title: Uncertainty in Action: Confidence Elicitation in Embodied Agents
contribution: Introduces elicitation and execution policies for embodied agents to express calibrated confidence in Minecraft tasks

title: SteerConf: Steering LLMs for Confidence Elicitation
contribution: Elicits confidence under steering prompts of varying caution and aggregates their consistency into calibrated scores

title: Evaluating Prompt Engineering Techniques for Accuracy and Confidence Elicitation in Medical LLMs
family: prompt engineering for medical confidence elicitation
contribution: Evaluates how prompt style, temperature and confidence scale affect elicited confidence of LLMs on medical board questions

title: Speaking in Self-Assessing Tongues: On the Verbalized Confidence of LLMs in Machine Translation
contribution: Devises verbalised methods for per-token confidence in machine translation and compares them with internal signals

title: Verbal Confidence Saturation in 3-9B Open-Weight Instruction-Tuned LLMs: A Pre-Registered Psychometric Validity Screen
contribution: Pre-registered psychometric screen finding verbal confidence of small instruct models saturates and fails item-level validity

title: How do LLMs Compute Verbal Confidence
contribution: Uses activation analyses to show verbal confidence is computed during answering and cached, reflecting more than token probability

title: The Mirage of Calibrated Confidence: Trajectory-Independence of Verbalized Confidence in Vision-Language Models
family: trajectory independence of verbalised confidence in VLMs
contribution: Shows verbalised confidence in VLMs ignores reasoning trajectory content and proposes a Trajectory-Grounding Score

title: Revisiting Uncertainty Estimation and Calibration of Large Language Models
family: numerical vs linguistic verbal uncertainty at scale
contribution: Evaluates token-probability, numerical verbal and linguistic verbal uncertainty over 80 models, favouring linguistic verbal uncertainty

title: Large Language Models Are Overconfident in Their Own Responses
contribution: Finds chat templates make models more confident in their own answers and reduces this by framing the answer as user input

title: Confidence Calibration and Rationalization for LLMs via Multi-Agent Deliberation
contribution: Training-free Collaborative Calibration in which multiple LLM agents deliberate to refine verbalised confidence and rationales

title: When Can We Trust LLM Graders? Calibrating Confidence for Automated Assessment
contribution: Compares self-reported, self-consistency and token confidence for LLM graders to route uncertain cases to human review
